brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Three full bases in a row, bolted together (2 joint bolts), with 14 end caps on the open faces. The build check passes with no mesh collisions.
handle:0,0,0;top sits on cover:0,0,0;full;top over the middle cell, so the caddy's weight is balanced either side of it. The configurator checks fit only, not how much weight the handle can carry.

requirements.requirement: Divided bins for screws and bits
requirements.evidence: bin:-1,0,0 and bin:1,0,0 are open hex-bin-full-div3 bins, 3 compartments each, 6 in total. bin:0,0,0 (2 compartments) is under the handle lid. In the staging, the left bin holds piles of M3 screws, nuts and standoffs, and so does the right bin. There is no bits prop, and a standing hex driver or hex key set would not fit there.

finish.summary: I built a three-cell tool caddy in a row: (-1,0,0), (0,0,0) and (1,0,0). The middle cell has a top cover with a carry handle on it. The two outer cells hold open full-depth bins with 3 compartments each, for screws and bits. Under the handle lid there is also a 2-compartment bin. All open faces are capped and the joints are bolted, for 31 parts in total. The build check passes with no rule issues and no mesh collisions. The prop catalog has no driver-bit prop, so all six compartments are staged with screw, nut and standoff piles. Standing a hex driver or hex key set in the right bin failed (the prop shifted or hit the bin wall).

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
